Lab CI/CD delivery

The lab pipeline delivers only the Linux proxy component. The macOS native worker is an external client: it follows the repository Git flow and its local Mac build/release guide, but it is not built, signed, or deployed by the lab runner.

Release contract​

Production delivery is tag-driven. Use the shared lab tag format:

prod-<major>.<minor>.<patch>[-<prerelease>]

For example, prod-2.1.0 runs validation, tests, the registry smoke test, builds the root Dockerfile once, pushes the image, updates the existing macocr-proxy Swarm service by immutable digest, and checks /healthz and /readyz. The service remains at one replica because WebSocket connections are owned by one proxy process.

dev-* and staging-* tags are accepted by the tag grammar for future lab environments. They do not deploy production. A tag is the only release trigger; ordinary merge-request and default-branch pipelines validate source changes but never update the live service.

Database migration gate​

Every prod-* tag runs migrate_prod_db after the registry smoke test and image build, but before the Swarm service update. The job runs the exact macocr-admin migrate binary from the immutable image digest on the Pi5 Swarm manager, attached only to the existing pg-net overlay network. It receives a protected MACOCR_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL variable through stdin; the URL is never written to the repository, image, job log, or a persistent host file.

The application currently uses one idempotent PostgreSQL schema migration function. The same function is used at application startup and by the explicit migration command, with a PostgreSQL advisory lock so a release job and a starting service cannot apply the schema concurrently. A migration failure blocks deployment. Tags for dev and staging do not touch production.

New schema changes must follow expand/contract compatibility: add or backfill before the new binary depends on a change, keep the previous image able to start during rollback, and defer destructive drops to a separately reviewed release. The migration job is therefore a release gate, not a second source of schema definitions.

GitLab variables​

These variables are provisioned at the GitLab global/instance scope when the lab control plane is available. Until then, the same names may be added at project scope for dungxbuif/mac-ocr. Secret variables must be masked and protected; the protected tag policy is the production gate.

VariablePurposeSecretRequired by
LAB_REGISTRY_HOSTregistry-gitlab.dungxbuif.comnoregistry/build
LAB_REGISTRY_PUSH_USERwrite deploy-token usernameyessmoke/build
LAB_REGISTRY_PUSH_PASSWORDwrite deploy-token valueyessmoke/build
LAB_REGISTRY_PULL_USERread deploy-token usernameyesSwarm deploy
LAB_REGISTRY_PULL_PASSWORDread deploy-token valueyesSwarm deploy
MACOCR_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URLproduction PostgreSQL URL for the one-shot migration commandyesmigration gate
MACOCR_SWARM_MANAGER_HOSTPi5 Swarm manager addressnodeploy
MACOCR_SWARM_MANAGER_USERSSH user on the managernodeploy
MACOCR_SWARM_SSH_PRIVATE_KEYprotected deployment keyyesdeploy
MACOCR_SWARM_KNOWN_HOSTSpinned SSH host key line(s)yesdeploy

The GitLab full-access PAT is an operator bootstrap credential only. It must not be placed in CI variables or passed to jobs. Use it to provision the least-privilege registry deploy tokens and runner, then keep it in the human secret store.

Runtime contract preserved by deployment​

The pipeline changes only the image of the existing Swarm service. It does not replace environment variables, mounts, replicas, health checks, or network attachments. The current service topology is:

  • edge-http-net for ingress;
  • macocr-redis-net for Redis;
  • pg-net for PostgreSQL/pgbouncer;
  • one replica, one CPU and one GiB limit, stop-first with rollback on update failure.

Keep runtime credentials out of the image. The existing service still has a follow-up migration from plain environment variables to versioned Swarm secrets; that migration is separate from this first CI/CD delivery and must be completed with a native-worker compatibility check before rotating the shared native authentication secret.

Registry smoke test and rollback​

Before building the application image, registry_smoke builds a scratch image, pushes it to the project registry, pulls it back, and verifies a digest. The smoke tag is unique to the pipeline and is removed locally; registry retention must clean these CI smoke tags.

The deploy job consumes the digest artifact from the build job and uses docker service update --with-registry-auth. Swarm's existing rollback policy remains in force. To roll back manually, update the service to the previous recorded digest; do not reuse a mutable latest tag.
